column11: the one approved tau PET tracer, priced per millicurie by Medicare's hospital outpatient system, taken at this agent's own dose. CMS OPPS Addendum B for CY2026, October 2026 update (www.cms.gov/files/zip/October-2026-OPPS-Addendum-B.zip, member 2026_October_Web_Addendum_B.10.14.26, read 2026-11-10): HCPCS A9601, 'Flortaucipir inj 1 millicuri', status indicator G, APC 0709, payment rate $371.000. NCT05641688 injects [18F]PI-2620 at 185 MBq, which is 5.0 millicuries at 37 MBq per millicurie, so a scan is 5 x $371.00 = $1,855.00
column12: the dose is this agent's own, from the registry; the rate is flortaucipir's, because no price for [18F]PI-2620 exists. Cross-check from the same file, where the three approved amyloid tracers are paid per study dose rather than per millicurie: florbetapir A9586 $1,825.64, flutemetamol Q9982 $1,944.01, florbetaben Q9983 $1,584.67. $1,855.00 lands inside that range. What this is NOT: the scan itself, which Medicare pays the hospital separately under APC 5593 and 5594 (CPT 78608, brain PET imaging, $1,460.92 in the same file) and which is never the manufacturer's revenue

column11: A9601 carries status indicator G, a pass-through drug or biological, and a pass-through item is paid under section 1833(t)(6)(D)(i) of the Social Security Act at the amount determined under section 1842(o), which is 106% of average sales price, the same basis as Part B. ASP is already net of the manufacturer's discounts and rebates, so the deduction is the statutory add-on, 6/106 = 0.056604 (backend/gross_to_net.py)
column12: weaker than the same figure on a Part B drug, and the number says why: $371.000 is round, which is what a rate set on wholesale acquisition cost looks like rather than one computed from an average sales price, and CMS prices a pass-through item with no ASP on file at wholesale acquisition cost plus 3% or at 95% of average wholesale price. If the rate is wholesale-based then the gross-to-net is a manufacturer discount nobody publishes, not a 6% add-on. The same Addendum also flags A9601's pass-through status as expiring during the calendar year, after which the code would be paid at mean unit cost from hospital claims, which carries no add-on at all. Treat the deduction as a placeholder of the right order, not a measurement

CMS Medicare Physician and Other Practitioners, by Geography and Service, national rows, place of service non-facility, the three amyloid tracers together: A9586 florbetapir 10,069 beneficiaries, Q9982 flutemetamol 2,681 and Q9983 florbetaben 6,434 in CY2024, 19,184 beneficiaries in all, against 1,189 in CY2023, 1,093 in CY2022 and 852 in CY2021. The sixteen-fold step sits on one policy date: CMS Medicare Coverage Database, NCD 220.6.20 (retired), version 2, 'Effective October 13, 2023, CMS removed NCD 220.6.20, ending CED for PET beta amyloid imaging and permitting Medicare coverage determinations for PET beta amyloid imaging to be made by the Medicare Administrative Contractors'. Those 19,184 are Medicare fee for service only, so they are grossed to all Medicare by the enrolment split in CMS Medicare Monthly Enrollment CY2024 (dataset d7fabe1e-d19b-4333-9eff-e80e0643f2fd): ORGNL_MDCR_BENES 33,913,847 of TOT_BENES 67,995,116, a 49.877% share, so 19,184 / 0.49877 = 38,463 scans a year. Over the 2,200,000 absolute label pool the eligible_pct above scales to: 0.017483. The multiple on the anchor is 1.0 and that is the judgement
column12: THIS IS A CEILING AND THE EVIDENCE AGAINST IT IS STRONGER THAN THE EVIDENCE FOR IT. Three measurements say a tau tracer does not reach amyloid PET's volume. (1) The approved tau tracer has essentially no clinical use. Flortaucipir (HCPCS A9601) returns zero rows in the CMS Physician and Other Practitioners file for every year CY2020 to CY2024, which under that file's rule means fewer than eleven beneficiaries nationally: 'any aggregated records which are derived from 10 or fewer beneficiaries are excluded'. The Physician/Supplier Procedure Summary, which has no such floor, carries 69 submitted millicuries in CY2024 and 580 in CY2025; at the label's 10 mCi dose that is about 7 scans and about 58 scans. No TAUVID revenue line appears in any Lilly 10-K after FY2020. (2) A four-state academic system performed none at all: Robb WH, Kaur G, Huang S et al., Alzheimers Dement 2026;22(4):e71343 (doi 10.1002/alz.71343, PMID 41950049, PMC13060759), Mayo Clinic enterprise electronic health record, January 2019 to March 2025: 'aducanumab (Aduhelm), donanemab (Kisunla), and tau PET (outside of research exams) were not utilized at Mayo Clinic during this time.' (3) An amyloid scan is required to start an anti-amyloid antibody and a tau scan is not, which is the whole reason amyloid PET inflected in 2024 and tau PET did not. AND THE SUBSTITUTE IS GROWING FASTER THAN THE THING IT SUBSTITUTES FOR: the same Mayo paper reports 'Abeta positron emission tomography scans increased (+22/quarter), cerebrospinal fluid biomarker orders declined (-25/quarter), and plasma p-tau217 orders rapidly increased (+238/quarter)'. THE CASE FOR THE CEILING, which is why I wrote it rather than a discount: amyloid PET itself ran at this book's pool for years before a policy change multiplied it sixteen-fold in one year, so a tau rate is a reimbursement question rather than a clinical one, and ADvance is the study that would answer it. TAUVID is approved only against histopathology and not for prognosis, which AC Immune states in its FY2025 20-F: 'it is approved only for a pathology indication (i.e. correlation with histopathology findings in Braak 5 and 6 patients), not for prognosis'. A reviewer who wants a discount should apply a multiple to this row and say what it is; I did not invent one
